qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the Delaware Division of Public Health for health programs and services funded by the Delaware Health Fund. It includes a detailed scope of services, submission deadlines, evaluation criteria, and contractual terms, clearly indicating a procurement opportunity.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT
This RFP is open to private organizations.
Statement of Need (§ II.A of proposal)-Delaware-specific evidence of the health need and the service gap the program fills; for returning organizations, including prior-year results.

findings.title: Subcontractors must be identified and approved
findings.fact: Proposed subcontractors must be identified in the proposal and approved by the Division of Public Health.

quotes.quote: The proposed subcontractors must be approved by the Division of Public Health. Proposed subcontractors must be identified in the proposal; any subcontractor engaged after award must be approved in advance by the Division.

findings.title: Business references required
findings.fact: Vendors must provide at least three business references of similar scope and value using Attachment 6.

quotes.quote: Provide  at  least  three  (3)  business  references  consisting  of  current  or  previous customers  of  similar  scope  and  value  using  Attachment  6.

findings.title: Transmittal letter must attest to data storage
findings.fact: The transmittal letter must attest that the Vendor shall not store or transfer non-public State of Delaware data outside of the United States.

quotes.quote: Furthermore, the transmittal letter must attest to the fact, at a minimum, that the Vendor shall not store or transfer non-public State of Delaware data outside of the United States.

findings.title: Exceptions must be recorded on Attachment 4
findings.fact: Any exceptions to the RFP must be recorded on Attachment 4, and acceptance is at the sole discretion of the evaluation committee.

quotes.quote: Any exceptions to the RFP, or the State of Delaware’s terms and conditions, must be recorded on Attachment 4. Acceptance of exceptions is within the sole discretion of the evaluation committee.

findings.title: Proposal Withdrawal Deadline
findings.fact: Vendor may modify or withdraw its proposal by written request, provided that both proposal and request is received by the State of Delaware prior to the proposal due date.

quotes.quote: Vendor may modify or withdraw its proposal by written request, provided that both proposal and request is received by the State of Delaware prior to the proposal due date.

findings.title: Proposal Expiration Date
findings.fact: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June 30, 2028.

quotes.quote: Prices quoted in the proposal shall remain fixed and binding on the bidder at least through June 30, 2028.

findings.title: Evaluation Committee Discretion on Exceptions
findings.fact: Acceptance of exceptions to the RFP is within the sole discretion of the evaluation committee.

quotes.quote: Acceptance of exceptions is within the sole discretion of the evaluation committee.

findings.title: Evaluation of Proposals Begins Shortly After Due Date
findings.fact: Evaluation of proposals is expected to begin shortly after the proposal due date.

quotes.quote: Evaluation  of  the  proposals  is  expected  to  begin shortly after the proposal due date.

findings.title: Oral Presentations May Be Required
findings.fact: Selected vendors may be invited to make oral presentations to the Evaluation Team, and their presentations will be scored or ranked.

quotes.quote: After initial scoring and a determination that vendor(s) are qualified to perform the required services, selected vendors may be invited to make oral presentations to the Evaluation Team. All vendor(s) selected will be given an opportunity to present to the Evaluation Team.

The selected vendors will have their presentations scored or ranked based on their ability to successfully meet the needs of the contract requirements, successfully demonstrate their product and/or service, and respond to questions about the solution capabilities.

findings.title: References and Site Visits
findings.fact: The Evaluation Team may contact any customer of the vendor, whether or not included in the vendor's reference list, and may visit existing installations.

quotes.quote: The Evaluation Team may contact any customer of the vendor, whether or not included in the vendor’s reference list, and use such information in the evaluation process. Additionally, the State of Delaware may choose to visit existing installations of comparable systems, which may or may not include vendor personnel.

findings.title: Clarification Process
findings.fact: The Evaluation Team may contact vendors to clarify uncertainties, but proposals may not be modified as a result of clarification requests.

quotes.quote: The Evaluation Team may contact any vendor in order to clarify uncertainties or eliminate confusion concerning the contents of a proposal. Proposals may not be modified as a result of any such clarification request.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria Encouragement
findings.fact: Vendors are encouraged to review evaluation criteria and provide detailed responses addressing each scored item.

quotes.quote: Vendors are encouraged to review the evaluation criteria and to provide a response that addresses each of the scored items. Evaluators will not be able to make assumptions about a vendor’s capabilities so the responding vendor should be detailed in their proposal responses.

findings.title: No Bid Bond or Performance Bond Required
findings.fact: There is no bid bond requirement and no performance bond requirement.

quotes.quote: There is no Bid Bond Requirement.
There is no Performance Bond requirement.

findings.title: Contract Execution Deadline
findings.fact: The successful vendor must execute the contract within twenty (20) days after award.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor shall promptly execute a contract incorporating the terms of this RFP within twenty (20) days after award of the contract.

findings.title: State's Right to Extend Contract
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to extend the contract on a month-to-month basis for up to three months after the full term.

quotes.quote: The State reserves the right to extend this contract on a month-to-month basis for a period of up to three months after the term of the full contract has been completed.

findings.title: Vendor Pricing Flexibility
findings.fact: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.

quotes.quote: Vendors are not restricted from offering lower pricing at any time during the contract term.

findings.title: Cooperative Use of Award
findings.fact: The contract may be used by other states and governmental entities through a participating addendum, but this places no obligation on the awarded vendor.

quotes.quote: As a publicly competed contract awarded in compliance with 29 DE Code Chapter 69, this contract is available for use by other states and/or governmental entities through a participating addendum. Interested parties should contact the State Contract Procurement Officer identified in the contract for instruction. Final approval for permitting participation in this contract resides with the Director of Government Support Services and in no way places any obligation upon the awarded vendor(s).

findings.title: Contract Use by Other Agencies
findings.fact: Covered agencies may procure under this contract if no state contract exists for the good or service, with agreement of all parties.

quotes.quote: If no state contract exists for a certain good or service, covered agencies may procure that certain good or service under another agency's contract so long as the arrangement is agreeable to all parties.

findings.title: Subscription License Costs
findings.fact: Subscription license costs are incurred only when utilized within a fully functioning solution; no costs during implementation; additional licenses above actual utilization may not exceed 5% of total.

quotes.quote: As a Service subscription license costs shall be incurred at the individual license level only as the individual license is utilized within a fully functioning solution. Subscription costs will not be applicable during periods of implementation and solution development prior to the State’s full acceptance of a working solution. Additional subscription license requests above actual utilization may not exceed 5% of the total and are subject to Delaware budget and technical review.

findings.title: Liquidated Damages
findings.fact: The State may include liquidated damages provisions for non-performance in the final contract.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may include in the final contract liquidated damages provisions for non-performance.

findings.title: Dispute Resolution
findings.fact: Disputes are to be resolved by negotiation, then mediation, then arbitration or litigation; each party bears its own costs; Delaware law and venue.

quotes.quote: At the option of the parties, they shall attempt in good faith to resolve any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement promptly by negotiation between executives who have authority to settle the controversy and who are at a higher level of management than the persons with direct responsibility for administration of this Agreement.

If the matter is not resolved by negotiation, as outlined above, or, alternatively, the parties elect to proceed directly to mediation, then the matter will proceed to mediation as set forth below. Any disputes, claims or controversies arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be submitted to a mediator selected by the parties. If the matter is not resolved through mediation, it may be submitted for arbitration or litigation. The Agency reserves the right to proceed directly to arbitration or litigation without negotiation or mediation. Any such proceedings held pursuant to this provision shall be governed by State of Delaware law, and jurisdiction and venue shall be in the State of Delaware. Each party shall bear its own costs of mediation, arbitration, or litigation, including attorneys’ fees.

findings.title: Covenant against Contingent Fees
findings.fact: Vendor warrants no contingent fees; breach allows State to annul contract or deduct full amount of such fees.

quotes.quote: The successful vendor will warrant that no person or selling agency has been employed or retained to solicit or secure this contract upon an agreement of understanding for a commission or percentage, brokerage or contingent fee excepting bona-fide employees, bona-fide established commercial or selling agencies maintained by the Vendor for the purpose of securing business. For breach or violation of this warranty the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul the contract without liability or at its discretion to deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: Personnel, Equipment and Services
findings.fact: Vendor must secure all personnel at own expense; equipment/services provided by vendor or under direct supervision; subcontracting requires prior written approval.

quotes.quote: The Vendor represents that it has, or will secure at its own expense, all personnel required to perform the services required under this contract.

None of the equipment and/or services covered by this contract shall be subcontracted without the prior written approval of the State. Only those subcontractors identified in Attachment 7 are considered approved upon award. Changes to those subcontractor(s) listed in Attachment 7 must be approved in writing by the State.

findings.title: Assignment of Antitrust Claims
findings.fact: Vendor assigns all antitrust claims to State regarding goods/services purchased under contract.

quotes.quote: As consideration for the award and execution of this contract by the State, the Vendor hereby grants, conveys, sells, assigns, and transfers to the State of Delaware all of its right, title and interest in and to all known or unknown causes of action it presently has or may now or hereafter acquire under the antitrust laws of the United States and the State of Delaware, regarding the specific goods or services purchased or acquired for the State pursuant to this contract.

findings.title: Payment Terms
findings.fact: State may pay by ACH or P-Card; payment within 30 days of correct invoice; vendors may offer discounts.

quotes.quote: The State reserves the right to pay by Automated Clearing House (ACH) or Purchase Card (P-Card). The agencies will authorize and process for payment of each invoice within thirty (30) days after the date of receipt of a correct invoice. Vendors are invited to offer in their proposal value added discounts (i.e. speed to pay discounts for specific payment terms). Cash or separate discounts should be computed and incorporated as invoiced.

findings.title: Additional Terms and Conditions
findings.fact: State reserves right to add terms and conditions during contract negotiations.

quotes.quote: Additional Terms and Conditions – The State of Delaware reserves the right to add terms and conditions during the contract negotiations.

findings.title: Eligibility limited to private organizations
findings.fact: This RFP is open to private organizations only; state-operated programs are not eligible to respond.
findings.business_implication: State-operated programs cannot apply for this funding; they must use a separate internal process. Private organizations have a clear opportunity but must ensure they meet this criterion.
findings.action_recommendation: Confirm that your organization is a private entity and not state-operated. If you are a state-operated program, do not submit a proposal; instead, follow the separate designation process.

quotes.quote: Eligibility:  This RFP is open to private organizations.  State-operated programs do not respond to this RFP; funding for state-operated programs is designated by the Department through a separate internal process pursuant to 16 Del. C. § 137(i)(1).

findings.title: Debarment and suspension ineligibility
findings.fact: Any entity currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder or any subcontractor is currently debarred or suspended, the proposal will be rejected. This is a hard stop.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that your organization and all proposed subcontractors are not currently debarred or suspended by any government entity. If any are, consider removing them or not bidding.

quotes.quote: Any  individual,  business,  organization,  corporation,  consortium,  partnership,  joint venture, or any other entity including subcontractors currently debarred or suspended is ineligible to bid.

findings.title: Ineligibility to conduct business in Delaware
findings.fact: Any entity ineligible to conduct business in the State of Delaware for any reason is ineligible to respond to the RFP.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is not authorized to do business in Delaware, they cannot bid. This includes lack of required registrations or licenses.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure your organization is authorized to conduct business in Delaware. If not, initiate the process to become authorized before submitting a proposal.

quotes.quote: Any entity ineligible to conduct business in the State of Delaware for any reason is ineligible to respond to the RFP.

findings.title: Exclusions based on criminal convictions and ethical violations
findings.fact: The Evaluation Team may refuse to consider proposals from vendors with certain criminal convictions, civil judgments, or ethical violations.
findings.business_implication: Even if not debarred, a vendor with certain criminal convictions or ethical violations may be disqualified. This could affect the bidder's reputation and eligibility.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the list of exclusions and assess if any of your organization's history or that of key personnel could trigger disqualification. If so, consider whether to bid or address the issues proactively.

quotes.quote: The Proposal Evaluation Team reserves the right to refuse to consider any proposal from a vendor who: a. Has  been  convicted  for  commission  of  a  criminal  offense  as  an  incident  to obtaining or attempting to obtain a public or private contract or subcontract, or in the performance of the contract or subcontract: b. Has  been  convicted  under  State  or  Federal  statutes  of  embezzlement,  theft,  forgery, bribery, falsification or destruction of records, receiving stolen property, or other  offense  indicating  a  lack  of  business  integrity  or  business  honesty  that currently and seriously affects responsibility as a State contractor: c. Has been convicted or has had a civil judgment entered for a violation under State or Federal antitrust statutes: d. Has violated contract provisions such as: 1)   Known   failure   without   good   cause   to   perform   in   accordance   with   the   specifications or within the time limit provided in the contract; or 2)   Failure to perform or unsatisfactory performance in accordance with terms of one or more contracts; e. Has violated ethical standards set out in law or regulation; and f. Any  other  cause  listed  in  regulations  of  the  State  of  Delaware  determined  to  be  serious and compelling as to affect responsibility as a State contractor, including suspension or debarment by another governmental entity for a cause listed in the regulations.

findings.title: State of Delaware business licensure required
findings.fact: Prior to award, the successful vendor must furnish proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the application process.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must have or be willing to obtain a Delaware business license before the contract is executed. This is a condition for award.
findings.action_recommendation: If you do not already have a Delaware business license, start the application process early to ensure you can provide proof or initiation before award. Include this in your proposal preparation timeline.

quotes.quote: Prior to the execution of an award document, the successful Vendor shall either furnish the Agency with proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the process of application where required.

Prior  to  receiving  an  award,  the  successful  vendor  shall  either  furnish  the  State  of Delaware with proof of State of Delaware Business Licensure or initiate the process of application where required.

findings.title: Minimum requirements include licenses and certifications
findings.fact: Vendors must provide Delaware licenses and/or certifications necessary to perform services as identified in the scope of work.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must hold or be able to obtain the required Delaware licenses and certifications before contract execution. Failure to do so will result in disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that all required Delaware licenses and certifications are current and in place, or initiate the application process immediately to ensure compliance by the proposal deadline.

quotes.quote: Provide Delaware license(s) and/or certification(s) necessary to perform services as identified in the scope of work.

findings.title: Prohibition on multiple proposals by primary vendor
findings.fact: A primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal in any form.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder intends to be a prime contractor, it cannot also appear as a partner or subcontractor in another proposal. This prevents conflicts and ensures commitment.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the bidder is not listed as a participant in any other proposal for this RFP, and confirm that all teaming arrangements comply with this restriction.

quotes.quote: A primary vendor may not participate in more than one proposal in any form.

findings.title: Joint venture requires prime contractor
findings.fact: Multi-vendor solutions are allowed only if one partner is designated as the prime contractor, and the State will not accept equal teaming arrangements.
findings.business_implication: If bidding as a joint venture, the bidder must clearly designate a prime contractor who will be the single point of contact and solely responsible for performance. Equal partnerships are not allowed.
findings.action_recommendation: If considering a joint venture, formalize the arrangement with a clear prime contractor and submit the joint venture agreement as required. Avoid any appearance of an equal teaming arrangement.

quotes.quote: Multi-vendor solutions (joint ventures) will be allowed only if one of the venture partners is designated as the “prime contractor”.
The State of Delaware will not accept any proposals that reflect an equal teaming arrangement or from vendors who are co-bidding on this RFP.

findings.title: Late proposals not accepted
findings.fact: Proposals submitted after the specified date and time will not be accepted.
findings.business_implication: Missing the submission deadline is an automatic disqualification. The proposal must be submitted via the Euna Procurement portal before the exact deadline.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit the proposal well in advance of the deadline to avoid technical issues. Confirm the exact date and time and ensure all required documents are uploaded correctly.

quotes.quote: Proposals submitted after the specified date and time will not be accepted by the Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) Portal.

findings.title: Non-conforming proposals may be rejected
findings.fact: Non-conforming proposals will not be considered; the State determines if a requirement is substantive or a formality.
findings.business_implication: The State has sole discretion to decide whether a deviation is substantive or a mere formality. Even minor non-compliance could lead to rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review all RFP requirements and ensure the proposal is fully compliant. If any requirement is unclear, seek clarification from the State before submission.

quotes.quote: Non-conforming proposals will not be considered. Non-conforming proposals are defined as those that do not meet the requirements of this RFP. The determination of whether an RFP requirement is substantive, or a mere formality shall reside solely within the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Vendor must be licensed to transact business in Delaware
findings.fact: The vendor shall be properly licensed and authorized to transact business in the State of Delaware as provided in 30 Del. C. § 2101.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be legally authorized to conduct business in Delaware, which may require obtaining a state business license. Failure to comply could result in fines, penalties, or disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify current Delaware business licensure status. If not licensed, initiate the application process immediately with the Delaware Division of Revenue to ensure compliance before award.

quotes.quote: The vendor shall be properly licensed and authorized to transact business in the State of Delaware as provided in 30 Del. C. § 2101.

findings.title: No Offshore Activity Requirement
findings.fact: Vendor must attest that no activity will take place outside the United States; failure to adhere is cause for elimination from future consideration.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure all work is performed within the United States, including any subcontractors or foreign offices. Violation could lead to elimination from the procurement process.
findings.action_recommendation: Review all operational locations and subcontractor arrangements to confirm no offshore activity. Include a formal attestation in the transmittal letter as required.

quotes.quote: No activity is to be executed in an offshore facility, either by a subcontracted firm or a foreign office or division of the vendor. The vendor must attest to the fact that no activity will take place outside of the United States in its transmittal letter. Failure to adhere to this requirement is cause for elimination from future consideration.

findings.title: Mandatory Submission Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals must include specified forms and information; failure to provide all appropriate information may deem the vendor non-responsive and exclude from further consideration.
findings.business_implication: Incomplete proposals will be rejected as non-responsive. The bidder must ensure all mandatory documents and information are included to avoid disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a checklist of all required submission items (transmittal letter, pricing, forms, etc.) and verify each is completed and included before submission. Double-check that all attachments are properly filled out.

quotes.quote: The items listed above provide the basis for evaluating each vendor’s proposal. Failure to provide all appropriate information may deem the submitting vendor as “non-responsive” and exclude the vendor from further consideration.

findings.title: Affirmation of No Suspension or Debarment
findings.fact: Vendor must affirm that within the past five years the firm and key individuals are not suspended or debarred.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must confirm that neither the company nor its key personnel have been suspended or debarred in the past five years. Any false affirmation could lead to contract termination or legal consequences.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct an internal review to ensure no suspensions or debarments exist. Prepare the affirmation statement and ensure it is signed by an authorized representative.

quotes.quote: The Vendor must affirm that within the past five (5) years the firm or any officer, controlling stockholder, partner, principal, or other person substantially involved in the contracting activities of the business is not currently suspended or debarred and is not a successor, subsidiary, or affiliate of a suspended or debarred business.

findings.title: Vendor Responsibility for Subcontractors
findings.fact: Successful vendor is responsible for all products and services; subcontractors must be identified and approved.
findings.business_implication: The bidder is fully responsible for all deliverables even if subcontracted. Subcontractors must be disclosed and approved by the state, and changes require written approval.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify all subcontractors and complete Attachment 7 for each. Ensure that all subcontractors comply with the same requirements and obtain necessary approvals before contract award.

quotes.quote: The successful Vendor(s) shall be responsible for all products and services as required by this RFP whether or not the Vendor or its subcontractor provided final fulfillment of the order. Subcontractors, if any, shall be clearly identified in the Vendor’s proposal by completing Attachment 7, and are subject the approval and acceptance of Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) Division of Public Health.

findings.title: Production Environment Requirement
findings.fact: All hardware and software must be in production use by at least three other customers for at least six months; unreleased or beta versions not acceptable.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that all proposed hardware and software products have a proven track record in production environments. This requirement may disqualify proposals that include cutting-edge or not-yet-fully deployed technologies, potentially limiting innovation but ensuring stability and reliability for the State.
findings.action_recommendation: Verify that all proposed products meet the production usage criteria. If any product is not yet generally available or lacks the required customer references, consider substituting with a compliant alternative or documenting an exception if allowed.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware requires that all hardware, system software products, and application software products included in proposals be currently in use in a production environment by at least three other customers, have been in use for at least six months, and have been generally available from the manufacturers for a period of six months. Unreleased or beta test hardware, system software, or application software will not be acceptable.

findings.title: Non-Collusion Statement Required
findings.fact: A complete and signed Non-collusion agreement must be included in the proposal.
findings.business_implication: Failure to include a signed non-collusion agreement could render the proposal non-responsive and lead to disqualification. This is a standard legal requirement to ensure fair competition and compliance with procurement regulations.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the non-collusion agreement is completed, signed by an authorized representative, and included in the submission package. Double-check that all required signatures are present before submission.

quotes.quote: One (1) complete and signed Non-collusion agreement (See Attachment 3 – in Appendix C)).

findings.title: Vendor Information Sheet Required
findings.fact: A completed Vendor Information Sheet must be included in the proposal.
findings.business_implication: The Vendor Information Sheet is a mandatory submission requirement. Omitting it may make the proposal non-responsive and exclude the bidder from consideration.
findings.action_recommendation: Complete the Vendor Information Sheet accurately, including all requested company details, and include it in the proposal package. Verify that all fields are filled out and the form is signed if required.

quotes.quote: One (1) completed Vendor information Sheet (See Attachment 2 – in Appendix C).

findings.title: Business References Required
findings.fact: A completed Business Reference form must be included; references other than State of Delaware contacts.
findings.business_implication: Providing business references is mandatory and helps the State evaluate the bidder's past performance and reliability. References from State of Delaware contacts are not acceptable, so the bidder must provide external references.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a list of at least three business references from clients other than the State of Delaware. Ensure the Business Reference form is fully completed with accurate contact information and include it in the proposal.

quotes.quote: One (1) completed Business Reference form (See Attachment 6 – in Appendix C)) – please provide references other than State of Delaware contacts – Form must be included.

findings.title: Exceptions Form Required
findings.fact: A completed RFP Exception form must be included; check box if no exceptions.
findings.business_implication: The RFP Exception form is mandatory. If the bidder has no exceptions to the RFP terms, they must still include the form and check the appropriate box. Failure to include it may lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP terms and conditions. If there are no exceptions, check the 'no exceptions' box on the form. If there are exceptions, list them clearly. Ensure the form is completed and included in the proposal package.

quotes.quote: One (1) completed RFP Exception form (See Attachment 4 – in Appendix C) – please check box if no information – Form must be included.

findings.title: Subcontractor Information Form Required if Applicable
findings.fact: A signed Subcontractor Information Form must be included for each subcontractor if applicable.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder intends to use subcontractors, failure to provide the required form for each will render the proposal non-responsive and disqualified.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify all subcontractors and ensure a signed Subcontractor Information Form is completed for each and included in the submission package.

quotes.quote: One (1) complete and signed copy of the Subcontractor Information Form (See Attachment 7 – in Appendix C)) for each subcontractor – only provide if applicable.

findings.title: Workplan Template Required
findings.fact: Completed Appendix E - Sample Workplan Template must be included.
findings.business_implication: The workplan is a mandatory submission; omission will make the proposal non-responsive and exclude the bidder from evaluation.
findings.action_recommendation: Complete the Appendix E - Sample Workplan Template thoroughly, ensuring it addresses all requirements and aligns with the RFP scope.

quotes.quote: Completed the Appendix E - Sample Workplan Template.

findings.title: Transmittal Letter Required
findings.fact: Transmittal letter as specified on page two must be included, including applicant's experience.
findings.business_implication: The transmittal letter is a mandatory component; missing it or omitting required experience details could lead to disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Draft a transmittal letter following the specifications on page two, explicitly stating the applicant's relevant experience in similar services.

quotes.quote: Transmittal Letter as specified on page two (2) of the Request for Proposal including an Applicant's experience, if any, providing similar services.

findings.title: Pricing Required
findings.fact: Pricing must be submitted as identified in the solicitation using Appendix F.
findings.business_implication: Pricing is a mandatory submission; failure to provide cost details using the specified template will render the proposal non-responsive.
findings.action_recommendation: Complete Appendix F – Project Cost Template accurately and include it in the submission, ensuring all pricing information is provided as required.

quotes.quote: Pricing as identified in the solicitation. Please submit your pricing/cost noted in Appendix F – Project Cost Template.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Online
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted online at the specified Bonfire portal.
findings.business_implication: Submissions must be made through the designated online portal; any other method may not be accepted, risking rejection.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal is uploaded to https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/ before the deadline, and verify successful submission.

quotes.quote: Proposals shall be submitted online at https://dhss.bonfirehub.com/

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.
findings.business_implication: This is a hard deadline; late submissions will not be accepted, risking disqualification.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all proposal documents are finalized and submitted through Euna Procurement well before the deadline to avoid technical issues.

quotes.quote: All proposals must be submitted prior to 1:00 PM EDT on September 15, 2026.

findings.title: Deadline for Receipt of Proposals
findings.fact: The deadline for receipt of proposals is September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT.
findings.business_implication: This is the official cutoff; any proposal received after this time will be rejected.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan to submit at least a few hours early to account for potential upload delays and confirm receipt via email confirmation.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Receipt of Proposals  Date: September 15, 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT

findings.title: Proposal Modifications Deadline
findings.fact: Changes, amendments, or modifications to proposals must be submitted through Euna Procurement prior to the proposal due date.
findings.business_implication: Once the deadline passes, no modifications are allowed, so the proposal must be complete and accurate at submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough internal review before submission and ensure all final changes are uploaded before the deadline.

quotes.quote: Any changes, amendments or modifications to a proposal must be submitted through Euna Procurement (formerly Bonfire) prior to the proposal due date.

findings.title: Evaluation of Proposals Schedule
findings.fact: The evaluation of proposals is scheduled from September 15 to October 9, 2026.
findings.business_implication: The evaluation period is relatively short, so the proposal must be clear and self-explanatory to facilitate quick review.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal is well-structured and addresses all evaluation criteria explicitly to aid evaluators during the limited review window.

quotes.quote:
Evaluation of Proposals  
Date: September 15 – October 9, 2026

findings.title: General Evaluation Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals are evaluated based on six criteria: Statement of Need, Alignment with Health Fund Priorities, Program Design and Feasibility, Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan, Organizational Capacity & Past Performance, and Budget Reasonableness and Sustainability.
findings.business_implication: The proposal must comprehensively address all six criteria to be competitive; missing any could significantly lower the score.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop the proposal with dedicated sections for each criterion, providing evidence and data to support claims, and ensure alignment with Delaware-specific health priorities.

quotes.quote:
B.  General Evaluation Requirements  
1.   Statement of Need (§ II.A of proposal)-Delaware-specific evidence of the health need and the service gap the program fills; for returning organizations, including prior-year results. 
2.   Alignment  with  Health  Fund  Priorities  (§  II.B)-fit  with  the  purposes  in  16  Del.  C.  §  137(d), with the strongest weight for direct ties to tobacco prevention and cessation and to cancer prevention, detection, and treatment. 
3.   Program  Design  and  Feasibility  (§  II.C)-goals,  activities,  timeline,  staffing,  and  geographic reach that are specific, coherent, and achievable within the contract year. 
4.   Measurable Outcomes and Evaluation Plan (§ II.D)-specific, verifiable objectives with indicators,  targets,  and  data  sources,  suitable  for  incorporation  into  the  award  agreement. 
5.   Organizational   Capacity   &   Past   Performance   (§   II.E)-governance,   financial   management, audit history, and experience operating programs of similar scope. 
6.   Budget  Reasonableness  and  Sustainability  (§  II.F)=  justified  costs  proportionate  to  reach,  documented  other  funding,  and  a  realistic  plan  given  declining  Master  Settlement Agreement revenue.

findings.title: Award Not Necessarily Based on Highest Score or Lowest Price
findings.fact: The contract will be awarded to the vendor whose proposal is most advantageous to the State, not necessarily the lowest bid or highest total point score.
findings.business_implication: Bidders cannot rely solely on offering the lowest price or achieving the highest technical score; the State retains discretion to select a proposal that it deems most advantageous overall, which may include considerations beyond price and score, such as strategic fit, past performance, or other qualitative factors.
findings.action_recommendation: In the proposal, emphasize the unique value proposition, alignment with the State's goals, and any differentiators that make the offer most advantageous, not just competitive pricing or high scores. Be prepared to justify how the proposal meets the State's broader objectives.

quotes.quote: It should be explicitly noted that the State of Delaware is not obligated to award the contract to the vendor who submits the lowest bid or the vendor who receives the highest total point score, rather the contract will be awarded to the vendor whose proposal is the most advantageous to the State of Delaware.

The Team reserves the right to: 
• Select for contract or for negotiations a proposal other than that with lowest costs.

findings.title: Contract Term and Funding Contingency
findings.fact: The contract term is one year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right.
findings.business_implication: The contract is for a single year only, and funding is not guaranteed beyond that period. The State is not obligated to renew, and continued funding depends on annual appropriations and a new RFP process. This creates uncertainty for long-term planning and revenue stability.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a one-year engagement with potential for recompete. Ensure the proposed budget and resource allocation are aligned with a 12-month performance period. Consider building flexibility into the proposal to accommodate potential changes in scope or funding in subsequent years.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation. Funding in subsequent fiscal years is not a renewal right: continued funding is subject to the annual statutory process under 16 Del. C. § 137(i), including the annual request for proposals, and to annual appropriation.

findings.title: Indemnification Obligations
findings.fact: The vendor must indemnify and hold harmless the State of Delaware from any liability arising out of the vendor's performance, and must indemnify against intellectual property infringement claims.
findings.business_implication: The vendor assumes significant financial risk, including potential liability for claims, attorney's fees, and costs, even if the claim is unsuccessful. This could expose the vendor to substantial unforeseen expenses and legal exposure.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review insurance coverage to ensure it is adequate to cover potential indemnification obligations. Consider negotiating limitations on indemnification, such as caps on liability or exclusions for consequential damages, where possible. Ensure that all subcontractors and personnel are covered by appropriate indemnities.

quotes.quote: By submitting a proposal, the proposing vendor agrees that in the event it is awarded a contract, it will indemnify and otherwise hold harmless the State of Delaware, its agents and employees from any and all liability, suits, actions, or claims, together with all costs, expenses for attorney’s fees, arising out of the vendor’s, its agents and employees’ performance work or services in connection with the contract.

Vendor shall warrant that all elements of its solution, including all equipment, software, documentation, services and deliverables, do not and will not infringe upon or violate any patent, copyright, trade secret or other proprietary rights of any third party. In the event of any claim, suit or action by any third party against the State of Delaware, the State of Delaware shall promptly notify the vendor in writing and vendor shall defend such claim, suit or action at vendor’s expense, and vendor shall indemnify the State of Delaware against any loss, cost, damage, expense or liability arising out of such claim, suit or action (including, without limitation, litigation costs, lost employee time, and counsel fees) whether or not such claim, suit or action is successful.

findings.title: Payment Terms and Authorization to Proceed
findings.fact: No work may begin until a purchase order signed by two authorized representatives is received, and payment is subject to appropriation.
findings.business_implication: The vendor cannot start work or incur costs until a formal purchase order is issued, which may cause delays. Additionally, payment is not guaranteed until funds are appropriated, adding financial risk.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a potential delay between award and contract execution. Do not begin work until the purchase order is received. Ensure that the proposal includes a clear timeline that accounts for this administrative step. Consider including a clause that allows for reimbursement of pre-award costs if the contract is ultimately not executed, if possible.

quotes.quote: No vendor is to begin any service prior to receipt of a State of Delaware purchase order signed by two authorized representatives of the agency requesting service, properly processed through the State of Delaware Accounting Office and the Department of Finance.
No contract or grant agreement will be executed, and no funds will be paid, unless and until such appropriation is enacted; contracts for funded awards are anticipated to begin July 1, 2028.

findings.title: Costs and Payment Schedules
findings.fact: All contract costs must be detailed in the Vendor's cost proposal; no charges other than as specified in the proposal shall be allowed without written consent. Payment schedule based on milestones; no advance payments; holdback up to 25% may be required.
findings.business_implication: The vendor must accurately estimate all costs upfront, as additional charges will not be permitted without written consent. Payments are tied to milestones, and up to 25% of contract monies may be withheld until acceptable performance is demonstrated, impacting cash flow.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a comprehensive and detailed cost proposal, ensuring all potential costs are included. Structure the payment schedule around clear, measurable milestones to facilitate timely payments. Be prepared to finance operations during the holdback period and ensure sufficient cash reserves.

quotes.quote: All contract costs must be detailed specifically in the Vendor’s cost proposal. No charges other than as specified in the proposal shall be allowed without written consent of the State of Delaware. The proposal costs shall include full compensation for all taxes that the selected vendor is required to pay.

The State of Delaware will require a payment schedule based on defined and measurable milestones. Payments for services will not be made in advance of work performed. The State of Delaware may require holdback of contract monies until acceptable performance is demonstrated (as much as 25%).

findings.title: Termination for Cause
findings.fact: State may terminate for cause with 20 days written notice; vendor has 5 days to respond; vendor may receive compensation for satisfactory work completed.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract for cause with only 20 days' notice, and the vendor has a very short 5-day window to respond and propose corrective actions. This creates significant risk of abrupt contract termination if performance issues arise, potentially leading to loss of revenue and reputation. However, the vendor is entitled to compensation for satisfactory work completed, which provides some financial protection.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure strict compliance with all contractual obligations to avoid triggering termination for cause. Develop internal processes to monitor performance and address any potential violations promptly. Prepare a contingency plan for responding to a termination notice within the 5-day window, including legal review and a clear corrective action proposal. Maintain thorough documentation of all work completed to support claims for compensation if termination occurs.

quotes.quote: If, for any reasons, or through any cause, the Vendor fails to fulfill in timely and proper manner its obligations under this Contract, or if the Vendor violates any of the covenants, agreements, or stipulations of this Contract, the State shall thereupon have the right to terminate this contract by giving written notice to the Vendor of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination. In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, maps, models, photographs, and reports or other material prepared by the Vendor under this Contract shall, at the option of the State, become its property, and the Vendor shall be entitled to receive just and equitable compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials which is usable to the State.
On receipt of the contract cancellation notice from the State, the Vendor shall have no less than five (5) days to provide a written response and may identify a method(s) to resolve the violation(s).

findings.title: Work Product Ownership
findings.fact: All materials and products developed under the contract are the sole and exclusive property of the State; vendor must seek written permission to use any product.
findings.business_implication: The State will own all work product, including any intellectual property developed during the contract. The vendor cannot reuse or exploit these materials for other purposes without explicit written permission, which could limit the vendor's ability to leverage the work for future business or build upon it. This may also affect the vendor's ability to use pre-existing tools or methodologies if they are incorporated into the deliverables.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the scope of 'materials and products' to understand what exactly will be owned by the State. If the vendor intends to use any pre-existing intellectual property, ensure it is clearly identified and licensed appropriately. Before contract execution, negotiate for a license back to the vendor for internal use or for use in other projects, if possible. Document all permissions obtained from the State for any external use of the work product.

quotes.quote: All materials and products developed under the executed contract by the vendor are the sole and exclusive property of the State. The vendor will seek written permission to use any product created under the contract.

findings.title: Contract Documents and Order of Precedence
findings.fact: Contract documents include RFP, purchase order, executed contract, and supplemental documents; order of precedence: contract, RFP, Vendor's response, purchase order.
findings.business_implication: The contract documents are hierarchical, with the executed contract taking precedence over the RFP and the vendor's response. This means that any inconsistencies between the vendor's proposal and the final contract will be resolved in favor of the contract. The vendor must ensure that the final contract accurately reflects all agreed terms and that no unintended discrepancies exist, as the contract will govern.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review the final contract document to ensure it aligns with the RFP and the vendor's proposal. Pay special attention to any modifications or additions in the contract that may differ from the original RFP. If there are discrepancies, address them before signing. Maintain a clear record of all documents and their versions to avoid confusion during contract performance.

quotes.quote: The RFP, the purchase order, the executed contract and any supplemental documents between the State of Delaware and the successful vendor shall constitute the contract between the State of Delaware and the vendor. In the event there is any discrepancy between any of these contract documents, the following order of documents governs so that the former prevails over the latter: contract, State of Delaware’s RFP, Vendor’s response to the RFP and purchase order. No other documents shall be considered. These documents will constitute the entire agreement between the State of Delaware and the vendor.

findings.title: Applicable Law and Jurisdiction
findings.fact: Delaware law applies; vendor consents to jurisdiction and venue in Delaware.
findings.business_implication: The contract will be governed by Delaware law, and any legal disputes must be resolved in Delaware courts. This could be inconvenient and costly for the vendor if they are not located in Delaware, as they may need to hire local counsel and travel for proceedings. It also means the vendor must be familiar with Delaware-specific legal requirements.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the implications of Delaware jurisdiction on the vendor's operations. If the vendor is not based in Delaware, consider the potential costs and logistics of litigating there. Ensure that the vendor's legal team is prepared to handle disputes under Delaware law. It may be prudent to consult with a Delaware attorney to understand any unique aspects of Delaware contract law that could affect the contract.

quotes.quote: The laws of the State of Delaware shall apply, except where Federal Law has precedence. The successful vendor consents to jurisdiction and venue in the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Access to Records and Audit
findings.fact: Vendor must maintain records for 5 years; State may inspect/audit; cost of audit disallowances borne by Vendor.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is required to retain all relevant records for five years and must allow the State to inspect and audit them. If the audit reveals disallowed costs, the vendor must reimburse the State from its own resources, which could result in significant financial liability. This imposes a heavy administrative burden and financial risk on the vendor.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust record-keeping systems to ensure all financial and performance records are accurate, complete, and retained for the required period. Establish internal audit procedures to proactively identify and correct any potential disallowances before a State audit. Set aside contingency funds to cover potential audit disallowances. Ensure that all costs charged to the contract are allowable and properly documented.

quotes.quote: The Vendor shall maintain books, records, documents, and other evidence pertaining to this Contract to the extent and in such detail as shall adequately reflect performance hereunder. The Vendor agrees to preserve and make available to the State, upon request, such records for a period of five (5) years from the date services were rendered by the Vendor.

The cost of any Contract audit disallowances resulting from the examination of the Vendor's financial records will be borne by the Vendor. Reimbursement to the State for disallowances shall be drawn from the Vendor's own resources and not charged to Contract cost or cost pools indirectly charging Contract costs.

findings.title: ACA Employer Liability Indemnification
findings.fact: If the State is determined to be a dual or sole employer of temporary staff, the vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State to the maximum extent of any liability.
findings.business_implication: The vendor bears significant financial and legal risk if the State is deemed an employer under the ACA, potentially facing substantial costs for penalties, legal fees, and damages. This could severely impact profitability and viability.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the likelihood of such a determination and consider negotiating caps on indemnification or requiring the State to share liability. Ensure robust ACA compliance and documentation to minimize risk. Obtain legal counsel to review the clause.

quotes.quote: In the event that the Internal Revenue Service, or any other third party governmental entity determines that the State of Delaware is a dual employer or the sole employer of any individual temporary staff person(s) provided to the State of Delaware pursuant to this Solicitation, Vendor agrees to hold harmless, indemnify, and defend the State to the maximum extent of any liability to the State arising out of such determinations.

findings.title: No Additional Insured Status for State
findings.fact: The State of Delaware shall not be named as an additional insured on any policy required under the agreement.
findings.business_implication: The State will not be covered under the vendor's insurance policies, meaning the vendor may be solely responsible for claims arising from its operations, potentially increasing its liability exposure.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that the vendor's own insurance coverage is adequate to cover potential liabilities without relying on the State's coverage. Consider obtaining additional coverage or umbrella policies to mitigate risks.

quotes.quote: In no event shall the State of Delaware be named as an additional insured on any policy required under this agreement.
The State of Delaware shall not be named as an additional insured.

findings.title: Warranty Obligation
findings.fact: Vendor must provide a one-year warranty and correct any defects at its own expense.
findings.business_implication: The vendor is obligated to fix any defects in deliverables for at least one year after acceptance, which could lead to significant post-implementation costs if issues arise.
findings.action_recommendation: Budget for potential warranty work and ensure thorough testing before acceptance. Clearly define what constitutes a defect and the scope of warranty coverage. Consider negotiating a shorter warranty period or limiting liability.

quotes.quote: The Vendor will provide a warranty that the deliverables provided pursuant to the contract will function as designed for a period of no less than one (1) year from the date of system acceptance. The warranty shall require the Vendor to correct, at its own expense, the setup, configuration, customizations or modifications so that it functions according to the State’s requirements.

findings.title: Non-discrimination as Material Breach
findings.fact: Failure to comply with non-discrimination provisions constitutes a material breach of contract.
findings.business_implication: Any violation of non-discrimination laws could be considered a material breach, allowing the State to terminate the contract and potentially seek damages, harming the vendor's reputation and finances.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement robust compliance programs to ensure adherence to all non-discrimination laws. Train staff and monitor practices to prevent violations. Have legal counsel review policies and procedures.

quotes.quote: Failure to perform under this provision constitutes a material breach of contract.

findings.title: Covenant against Contingent Fees
findings.fact: The State may annul the contract or deduct the full amount of any contingent fee if the Vendor breaches the warranty against contingent fees.
findings.business_implication: If the vendor has engaged in contingent fee arrangements (e.g., paying commissions to secure the contract), the State can cancel the contract without liability or recover the full fee amount, leading to financial loss and contract termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure that no contingent fees are paid to secure the contract. Review all agreements with agents or brokers to confirm compliance. If any such fees exist, disclose them and seek legal advice.

quotes.quote: For breach or violation of this warranty the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul the contract without liability or at its discretion to deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: Vendor Responsibility for Subcontractors
findings.fact: The Vendor is responsible for all products and services, including those provided by subcontractors.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears full responsibility for the performance and compliance of any subcontractors, even if the subcontractor fails to deliver. This could lead to financial losses, penalties, or contract termination if subcontractors underperform or violate terms.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully vet and select subcontractors, ensure they are clearly identified in the proposal (Attachment 7), and include robust contractual clauses to hold them accountable. Monitor subcontractor performance closely and maintain contingency plans.

quotes.quote: The successful Vendor(s) shall be responsible for all products and services as required by this RFP whether or not the Vendor or its subcontractor provided final fulfillment of the order.

findings.title: Background Check Violation
findings.fact: Violation of background check requirements may subject the Vendor to penalty, including contract cancellation for cause.
findings.business_implication: Non-compliance with background check requirements can lead to severe consequences, including contract termination and potential financial penalties. This could damage the bidder's reputation and result in loss of the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a rigorous background check process for all employees and subcontractors who will access state property or interact with vulnerable populations. Maintain records of checks and certifications, and ensure any individuals listed on registries are barred from direct contact or obtain waivers as needed.

quotes.quote: A violation of this condition represents a violation of the contract terms and conditions, and may subject the Vendor to penalty, including contract cancellation for cause.

findings.title: Work Product Ownership
findings.fact: All materials and products developed under the contract are the sole and exclusive property of the State.
findings.business_implication: The bidder will not retain any intellectual property rights to work products created under the contract. This could limit the bidder's ability to reuse or commercialize the developed materials for other clients or purposes.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the scope of 'materials and products' and negotiate for a license to use the work product for internal purposes or future projects. Ensure that any pre-existing IP is clearly identified and protected. Seek written permission before using any contract deliverables.

quotes.quote: All materials and products developed under the executed contract by the vendor are the sole and exclusive property of the State.

findings.title: Non-compliance with Laws
findings.fact: Failure to comply with specified laws may result in the State disregarding the proposal, terminating the contract, or considering the vendor in default.
findings.business_implication: Any non-compliance with applicable laws (including federal, state, and local) can lead to immediate disqualification, contract termination, or being declared in default. This poses a significant risk to the bidder's business and legal standing.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough legal review to ensure full compliance with all applicable laws, including civil rights, equal employment, and ADA. Maintain ongoing compliance monitoring and designate a compliance officer to oversee adherence throughout the contract period.

quotes.quote: If any vendor fails to comply with a through e (noted above) of this paragraph, the State of Delaware reserves the right to disregard the proposal, terminate the contract, or consider the vendor in default.

findings.title: IRS 1075 Compliance and Penalties
findings.fact: Failure to comply with FTI safeguards may result in contract voidance and criminal/civil penalties.
findings.business_implication: Non-compliance with IRS 1075 and FTI safeguards can lead to contract voidance, severe criminal penalties (fines up to $5,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years) and civil damages. This could have catastrophic financial and reputational consequences for the bidder.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a comprehensive FTI safeguarding program, including employee training, written notifications, and annual recertifications. Ensure all personnel handling FTI understand the legal requirements and penalties. Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance and maintain documentation.

quotes.quote: The agency will have the right to void the contract if the contractor fails to meet the terms of FTI safeguards described herein.

Each officer or employee of a contractor to whom FTI is or may be disclosed shall be notified in writing that FTI disclosed to such officer or employee can be used only for a purpose and to the extent authorized herein, and that further disclosure of any FTI for a purpose not authorized herein constitutes a felony punishable upon conviction by a fine of as much as $5,000 or imprisonment for as long as 5 years, or both, together with the costs of prosecution.

findings.title: Assignment Restriction
findings.fact: The contract cannot be assigned without prior written consent from the Agency.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot transfer its rights or obligations under the contract to a third party without the Agency's prior written consent. This could restrict corporate restructuring, acquisitions, or subcontracting arrangements, and may limit flexibility in managing the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the assignment clause carefully and consider whether any potential future assignments (e.g., merger, acquisition, or subcontracting) are anticipated. If so, seek clarification or negotiate for more flexible assignment rights, or ensure that any required consents are obtained in advance.

quotes.quote: Any resulting contract shall not be assigned except by express prior written consent from the Agency.

findings.title: Changes Require Written Consent
findings.fact: No alterations to terms, conditions, delivery, price, quality, or specifications are effective without written consent.
findings.business_implication: Any changes to the contract terms, including pricing, delivery schedules, or specifications, must be formally approved in writing by the State. This could create delays if changes are needed, and the bidder may be unable to adjust terms without the State's cooperation.
findings.action_recommendation: Establish a clear process for requesting and documenting changes, and ensure that all modifications are formally approved in writing before implementation. Proactively communicate any potential changes to the State to avoid disputes.

quotes.quote: No alterations in any terms, conditions, delivery, price, quality, or specifications of items ordered will be effective without the written consent of the State of Delaware.

findings.title: Additional Terms and Conditions
findings.fact: The State reserves the right to add terms and conditions during contract negotiations.
findings.business_implication: The State may introduce new terms and conditions during negotiations, which could alter the commercial or legal balance of the contract. This introduces uncertainty and may require the bidder to accept terms that were not initially anticipated.
findings.action_recommendation: Be prepared to negotiate additional terms and conditions. Clearly define the scope of acceptable changes and ensure that any new terms are carefully reviewed for their impact on pricing, liability, and performance obligations.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware reserves the right to add terms and conditions during the contract negotiations.

findings.title: State's Right to Cancel Solicitation
findings.fact: The State of Delaware reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time during the procurement process, for any reason or for no reason.
findings.business_implication: The State can cancel the solicitation at any time without cause, meaning the bidder may incur costs in preparing a proposal that could be wasted if the solicitation is cancelled. There is no guarantee that a contract will be awarded.
findings.action_recommendation: Assess the risk of cancellation and limit investment in proposal preparation until the award is certain. Consider including a clause in the proposal to recover costs if the solicitation is cancelled, though this may not be accepted.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware reserves the right to cancel this solicitation at any time during the procurement process, for any reason or for no reason.

findings.title: State's Right to Terminate Negotiations
findings.fact: The State of Delaware may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.
findings.business_implication: Even if the bidder is selected for negotiations, the State can walk away without any obligation. This means the bidder may invest time and resources in negotiations without a guarantee of a contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Keep negotiation efforts efficient and avoid making significant commitments until a contract is signed. Clarify the negotiation process and any milestones to minimize wasted effort.

quotes.quote: The State of Delaware may terminate negotiations at any time and for any reason, or for no reason.

findings.title: Evaluation Team May Terminate Negotiations
findings.fact: The Proposal Evaluation Team may, at its discretion, terminate negotiations with any or all vendors.
findings.business_implication: The State has the unilateral right to end negotiations at any time, meaning the bidder's proposal may be rejected without recourse, and the bidder could incur costs in preparing and negotiating without guarantee of award.
findings.action_recommendation: Bidders should be prepared for the possibility of termination and avoid incurring significant non-recoverable costs until a contract is signed. Maintain flexibility and be ready to respond quickly to negotiation requests.

quotes.quote: The Team may negotiate with one or more vendors during the same period and may, at its discretion, terminate negotiations with any or all vendors.

findings.title: Annulment of Award for Failure to Enter Agreement
findings.fact: If the vendor to whom the award is made fails to enter into the agreement, the award will be annulled, and an award may be made to another vendor.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be fully prepared to execute the contract within the specified timeframe (20 days) after award; any delay or failure could result in losing the award and potential liability for costs incurred by the State in re-awarding.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure all internal approvals and resources are in place to sign the contract promptly upon award. Review the contract terms in advance and have legal counsel ready to expedite the signing process.

quotes.quote: If the vendor to whom the award is made fails to enter into the agreement as herein provided, the award will be annulled, and an award may be made to another vendor.

findings.title: State's Right to Annul Contract for Lobbying or Gratuities
findings.fact: The State of Delaware shall have the right to annul any contract resulting from this RFP without liability for breach of warranty against lobbying or gratuities.
findings.business_implication: Any violation of lobbying or gratuity prohibitions can lead to immediate contract annulment without liability to the State, potentially resulting in loss of revenue and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement strict internal policies to ensure no lobbying or provision of gratuities to State employees. Train all personnel involved in the RFP process on these prohibitions and monitor compliance.

quotes.quote: For breach or violation of this warranty, the State of Delaware shall have the right to annul any contract resulting from this RFP without liability or at its discretion deduct from the contract price or otherwise recover the full amount of such commission, percentage, brokerage or contingent fee.

findings.title: Termination for Cause
findings.fact: The State may terminate the contract for cause if the Vendor fails to fulfill its obligations or violates any covenants, with at least 20 days written notice. The Vendor has at least 5 days to respond and propose a corrective action plan, but the State may reject it and proceed with termination.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract for any failure to perform, and the vendor's ability to cure is limited; the State can reject the vendor's corrective plan and proceed with termination, leaving the vendor with no further recourse.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain high performance standards and ensure all contractual obligations are met. If a default occurs, respond within the 5-day window with a robust corrective action plan, but also be prepared for the possibility of termination and mitigate potential damages.

quotes.quote: If, for any reasons, or through any cause, the Vendor fails to fulfill in timely and proper manner its obligations under this Contract, or if the Vendor violates any of the covenants, agreements, or stipulations of this Contract, the State shall thereupon have the right to terminate this contract by giving written notice to the Vendor of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination.

On receipt of the contract cancellation notice from the State, the Vendor shall have no less than five (5) days to provide a written response and may identify a method(s) to resolve the violation(s). A vendor response shall not affect or prevent the contract cancellation unless the State provides a written acceptance of the vendor response. If the State does accept the Vendor’s method and/or action plan to correct the identified deficiencies, the State will define the time by which the Vendor must fulfill its corrective obligations. Final retraction of the State’s termination for cause will only occur after the Vendor successfully rectifies the original violation(s). At its discretion the State may reject in writing the Vendor’s proposed action plan and proceed with the original contract cancellation timeline.

findings.title: Termination for Convenience
findings.fact: The State may terminate the contract at any time for convenience with at least 20 days written notice. The Vendor is entitled to compensation for satisfactory work completed that is usable to the State.
findings.business_implication: The State can terminate the contract without cause, leaving the vendor with only compensation for work completed that is usable to the State, which may not cover all costs or lost profits.
findings.action_recommendation: Maintain detailed records of all work performed and deliverables to ensure proper compensation in case of termination. Consider negotiating for more favorable termination compensation terms, such as payment for all work in progress and reasonable profit.

quotes.quote: The State may terminate this Contract at any time by giving written notice of such termination and specifying the effective date thereof, at least twenty (20) days before the effective date of such termination. In that event, all finished or unfinished documents, data, studies, surveys, drawings, models, photographs, reports, supplies, and other materials shall, at the option of the State, become its property and the Vendor shall be entitled to receive compensation for any satisfactory work completed on such documents and other materials, and which is usable to the State.

findings.title: Termination for Failure to Submit Reports
findings.fact: Failure to submit required reports may result in corrective action, up to and including possible cancellation of the award.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure strict compliance with monthly reporting obligations to avoid corrective action, including cancellation of the award. Non-compliance could also negatively impact future proposal evaluations.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust reporting system to ensure timely and accurate submission of all required reports (Attachments 8 and 9) in the specified format. Assign a dedicated team to monitor deadlines and content.

findings.title: Subcontracting Allowed Statement Contradiction
findings.fact: The RFP contains contradictory statements regarding subcontracting: one section states 'The use of subcontractors WILL be permitted for this project', while another section states 'Services specified in the proposal shall not be subcontracted without prior written approval by the State of Delaware'.
findings.business_implication: The contradiction creates ambiguity about the permissibility of subcontracting. Bidders may be unsure whether they can rely on subcontractors and under what conditions.
