findings.title: Contract Term Contradiction
findings.fact: The RFP states the contract term is one year (July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028) but also mentions a Fiscal Year 2029 RFP and a streamlined continuation response, implying a possible multi-year program.
findings.business_implication: The apparent contradiction between a one-year contract term and the mention of a Fiscal Year 2029 RFP suggests that while the initial contract is for one year, there may be an opportunity for continued funding through a streamlined process. This could affect the bidder's pricing strategy, resource allocation, and long-term planning. The bidder should be prepared for a potential multi-year engagement but must also recognize that continued funding is not guaranteed and is subject to annual appropriation and a new RFP process.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the procuring agency whether the contract is intended to be a single-year engagement with a possible streamlined renewal, or if there is an expectation of a multi-year program. Adjust the proposal to reflect a one-year base contract with options for renewal, and ensure pricing and staffing plans are flexible to accommodate potential continuation. Also, monitor the release of the Fiscal Year 2029 RFP and prepare a streamlined continuation response if applicable.

quotes.quote: Contract term is one (1) year, anticipated July 1, 2027 through June 30, 2028, contingent on appropriation.

Organizations funded in Fiscal Year 2028 that seek Fiscal Year 2029 funding must respond to the Fiscal Year 2029 RFP (anticipated release on or before July 1, 2027), which is expected to include a streamlined continuation response for organizations proposing to continue substantially the same program.

findings.title: Contract Document Hierarchy Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP states that the contract documents hierarchy is contract, RFP, vendor response, purchase order, but also states that the RFP and vendor response will be incorporated into the formal contract, creating ambiguity about precedence.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity regarding the precedence of contract documents could lead to disputes during contract execution. If the RFP and vendor response are incorporated into the contract, it is unclear whether they are subordinate to the contract or if they take precedence. This could affect the interpretation of terms and conditions, potentially impacting the bidder's rights and obligations.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from the procuring agency on the exact hierarchy of documents and how the incorporation of the RFP and vendor response will affect precedence. Ensure that the vendor response is carefully drafted to align with the RFP and the contract, and consider including a provision in the contract that clearly defines the order of precedence to avoid future disputes.

quotes.quote: This RFP and the selected vendor’s response to this RFP will be incorporated as part of any formal contract.

In the event there is any discrepancy between any of these contract documents, the following order of documents governs so that the former prevails over the latter: contract, State of Delaware’s RFP, Vendor’s response to the RFP and purchase order.

findings.title: Subcontractor Approval Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP states that only subcontractors identified in Attachment 7 are considered approved upon award, but also states that subcontractors are subject to approval and acceptance of DHSS Division of Public Health, creating ambiguity about the approval process.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity regarding subcontractor approval could lead to misunderstandings about the approval process. If the bidder plans to use subcontractors, they need to know whether listing them in Attachment 7 is sufficient for approval or if additional approval is required. This could affect the bidder's ability to subcontract work and may impact the project timeline if approvals are delayed.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify with the procuring agency whether listing subcontractors in Attachment 7 constitutes final approval or if additional approval is required. Ensure that all subcontractors are clearly identified in the proposal and that any changes to subcontractors are communicated and approved in writing. Also, confirm the approval process and timeline to avoid delays.

quotes.quote: Subcontractors, if any, shall be clearly identified in the Vendor’s proposal by completing Attachment 7, and are subject the approval and acceptance of Department of Health and Social Services (DHSS) Division of Public Health.
Only those subcontractors identified in Attachment 7 are considered approved upon award. Changes to those subcontractor(s) listed in Attachment 7 must be approved in writing by the State.
